files.purpose: The chat screen's root view and its floating-panel layout engine: lays out the timeline, composer and up to five kinds of floating panels (subagent, Hydra team, popped-out head, auto-popped heads, usage) around the conversation column, computing docking, stacking, reserve padding and slide animations for each. It also hosts the sticky glass chrome row (thread list/new-thread/Hydra/permission/branch buttons, the thread title with its rename popover, and the open-in/scripts/git-actions and terminal/changes capsules) plus the commit and project-scripts editor sheets reached from that row.
state_owned: GitStatusModel: a per-directory, cross-chat git status/branch/remote-URL cache with a 30s freshness window
subagentDrag / hydraDrag / poppedDrag / usageDrag / autoDrag PanelDragState, plus autoDrags: [UUID: PanelDragState]
panelResize: PanelResizeState (live grip-resize size and usage-panel height)
hydraShownSince / hydraLingers / hydraLingerTask (the Hydra panel's post-heads linger timer)
side_effects: Spawns async Tasks: git refresh on directory or diffRevision change, and the Hydra-linger delay task
NSPasteboard writes (copy thread title, copy directory path)
NSWorkspace.shared.open for Finder, installed editors and the repository URL
Presents sheets (CommitSheet, ScriptsEditor) and alerts (rename thread, new branch)
Calls into AppModel for thread/subagent/Hydra lifecycle and project script mutation
Under a capture-tool launch flag only, publishes this view's on-screen frames to WebsiteCaptures
platform_assumptions: GlassEffectContainer / .chromeGlassCircle / .glassEffect for the chrome row and floating panels' Liquid Glass rendering
Traffic-light clearance padding (Chrome.trafficLightsWidth) tied to macOS window chrome when the sidebar does not hold the window buttons
persisted_fields: project.scripts (via ScriptsEditor save), thread title (via rename)
ui_elements: Chrome row: Threads button, New-thread button, HydraButton, PermissionMenu, BranchMenu, ChatChromeTitle (with copy/rename popover), Open-in capsule (Finder/editors/copy path), Scripts capsule, Git-actions capsule (commit/push/PR/open repo), Terminal and Changes toggle capsule
Jump-to-latest floating button
Five floating panel kinds (subagent, Hydra team, popped head, auto-popped heads, usage) each with a drag handle and resize grips
CommitSheet (message editor, write-for-me, push-after-commit toggle)
ScriptsEditor sheet (per-script name/command/run-on-worktree-create rows)
feature_notes: B2->B3 replaces two internal `WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled` reads (HydraCaptureFrame's body guard at B3 line 408, and ThreadsButton's capture-still hook at B3 line 1262) with `CaptureRun.isEnabled` directly. WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled already forwarded to CaptureRun.isEnabled in B2 (confirmed by diffing App/Captures/WebsiteCaptures.swift, which drops its own isEnabled/outputDirectory/storageRoot/defaults wrapper properties and points every call site at CaptureRun.* directly instead), so this is a pure internal refactor with no observable effect. The port already excludes the whole capture subsystem (spec record PR-CHAT-174, decision ED-001), so port scope is unaffected.

files.purpose: The chat's Hydra mark button in the chrome row: shows whether the team is on for this thread, animates a rotating multi-colour charge ring plus a breathing glow while any head is at work, badges the sending/working head count, and opens or explains the floating team panel. A large part of the file is HydraChargeLayerView, a hand-built Core Animation layer view that drives the ring-turn and glow-breathe animations off the render server (rather than as SwiftUI animations) so a working team costs the main thread nothing.
calls_into: NSEvent local event monitor for right-click/control-click detection
state_owned: HydraButton.delegationChecks and .streamingScans: static, per-timeline-row caches (RecentCache limit 32, dictionary capped at 64) memoizing whether a finished or streaming reply holds a delegation block
HydraChargeLayerView's CAGradientLayer pair (glow, ring) and their installed CABasicAnimations, kept on a shared clock origin so re-installing them never changes phase
side_effects: Installs/removes an NSEvent local monitor per button instance for secondary clicks, torn down on window change or deinit
Starts a 0.9s Task to clear the 'sending' pulse after heads go out
Registers for NSApplication.didBecomeActiveNotification, NSWindow.didChangeOcclusionStateNotification and ThemeManager.didChange to reinstall or recolour the Core Animation layers
platform_assumptions: NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEvents for secondary-click detection, since a SwiftUI Button in front claims every left-click hit
CALayer/CAGradientLayer/CAShapeLayer driven directly with explicit CABasicAnimations for render-server-side, main-thread-free animation
NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion gates the still vs. moving charge
.chromeGlassCircle() / .popover for the button's glass chrome and its three popovers
ui_elements: The 18x18 dragon-head mark, dim at rest and full opacity on hover or when on
The rotating ring + breathing glow charge (HydraCharge) and its top-trailing working/sending count badge
HydraIdlePopover (290pt explainer when Hydra is on but nothing is out)
HydraSwitchPopover (per-chat Hydra on/off menu, right-click)
HydraIntroPopover (first-run explainer, opened from here but defined in a separate file)
feature_notes: B2->B3's only change is the same internal rename seen in ChatView.swift: the geometry-change guard that reports the mark's on-screen frame to the website-captures tool now reads `CaptureRun.isEnabled` instead of `WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled` (line 96). Both were equivalent in B2, so there is no observable behaviour change, and no spec record's cited line range (the closest HYDRA.json citations sit at :89-92, immediately before this edit) overlaps it.

files.purpose: Three small header-plus-scroll popovers used off a Hydra head's pill or brief: a shared header row (glyph, name with status caption, task, trailing accessory), a finished head's markdown report popover (opened from its pill, with a copy button), and the lead's brief-to-a-head popover (opened from the brief itself, also with a copy button). Both content popovers lay out every markdown block eagerly inside a fixed-width PopoverScroll so the popover opens at its final size instead of growing after it appears.
platform_assumptions: SwiftUI .popover sizing (the eager block layout inside PopoverScroll exists specifically so the popover does not visibly grow after opening)
textSelection(.enabled) for native text selection in the report/brief body
ui_elements: HydraPopoverHeader: 28pt glyph, name+status caption row, optional 3-line task, trailing accessory slot
HydraHeadReportPopover: 460pt wide, header over a divider, 'No report yet.' placeholder or markdown blocks scrolling to a 460pt max height
HydraBriefPopover: 520pt wide, same layout with no placeholder branch (a brief always has text)
feature_notes: B2->B3 replaces HydraHeadReportPopover.duration(from:to:)'s own hand-rolled three-tier formatter (seconds clamped at zero; "Ns" under a minute, "M min" under an hour, "H h M min" beyond) with a call to the shared `RelativeTime.duration(_:)` helper (UI/Common/Components.swift). That helper's exact format is already established elsewhere in this same spec/port as "Ns" / "Mm Ss" / "Hh Mm" (porting/spec/CHAT.json's record for Components.swift:36-41, and the already-ported Marrow.UI.Common.RelativeTime.Duration in src/Marrow.UI/Common/Components.cs) -- a different string shape from the retired algorithm for the middle and top tiers: "7 min" becomes "7m 0s", and "2 h 14 min" becomes "2h 14m". This is a genuine, user-visible change to the head-report popover's 'Finished/Failed/Stopped · <duration>' caption. The C# port of this file (src/Marrow.App/Views/Chat/HydraHeadPopovers.cs) is an unimplemented skeleton -- its Duration() stub still throws NotImplementedException and its file-header comment still pins 'B2 1fbf81e' -- so nothing already-built needs correcting, but the eventual implementation must call the existing RelativeTime.Duration equivalent rather than reproduce the retired three-tier scheme, and the file-header source pin needs updating to the B3 commit when the unit is picked up.
unresolved_questions: Confirm the exact narrow-width Duration.formatted() output against the compiled B3 reference app (or an authoritative description of Apple's UnitsFormatStyle narrow width) before finalizing PR-HYDRA-214's expected_result strings; this report relies on the already-established RelativeTime.duration precedent recorded elsewhere in the spec/port rather than an independent runtime check of this exact call site.

files.purpose: The floating 'team' glass panel: a single head's live conversation (or, in compact mode, its progress bar) on stage in the middle, a draggable top strip that counts the heads and opens a popover to switch stage or stop one, buttons to pop the on-stage head out into its own panel or dismiss the whole panel, and a finish 'wave' overlay that holds a just-finished head on stage for a fixed hold time before another can take over. The back half of the file supplies the presentation logic and exact wording the strip, footer and popover rows all read from: HydraStatusText's three text registers and HydraLiveInfo's live-overlay rule.
calls_into: ThreadTimeline / ComposerArea (a Droppy-run head's own chat box)
state_owned: hold: StageHold? (@State) -- the finished-head wave timer, keyed by (head id, startedAt)
side_effects: A `.task(id: hold)` sleeps HydraPanel.finishHold (2.0s) then clears the hold with an animation
HydraStopButton and the popover's 'Stop all heads'/'Clear finished heads' items call into AppModel to stop or clear heads
platform_assumptions: .glassEffect(.regular, in: shape) plus a separate filled-and-shadowed backing shape for the panel's Liquid Glass look (the file documents this split as deliberate: one shadow on a plain fill rather than re-blurring the glass on every streamed token)
DotFieldSweep as a Core-Animation-driven 'done' wave tinted with the finished head's persona colour
persisted_fields: reads runtime.hydraSelectedHeadID / hydraWaitingCount and model.settings.hydraShowsHeadDetails; no fields owned here (dock/stack-order state lives in ChatView/ThreadRuntime)
ui_elements: The panel itself (22pt corner radius, size handed in by PanelScene)
Its top strip: head-count capsule (HydraHeadsButton), the on-stage name/status/provider/elapsed-time capsule that also drags the panel, pop-out and dismiss circle buttons
The heads popover: per-head rows with a stop button while running, 'Stop all heads' and 'Clear finished heads' items
The native-head footer: spinner or outcome glyph, status text, step count
feature_notes: B2->B3 has one functional change: HydraStatusText.elapsed(_:) now builds its ' in <duration>' clause with `Duration.seconds(seconds).formatted(.units(allowed: [.seconds, .minutes], width: .narrow, maximumUnitCount: 2, fractionalPart: .hide(rounded: .down)))` instead of the retired `seconds < 60 ? " in Ns" : " in Mm Ss"` string interpolation. Because this allowed-unit set omits .hours (unlike the sibling RelativeTime.duration, which includes hours and is already an established source fact elsewhere in this spec/port as 'Ns'/'Mm Ss'/'Hh Mm'), the narrow-width formatter restricted to seconds+minutes very likely still renders exactly 'Ns' below a minute and 'Mm Ss' at or above with no hour rollover for any duration -- i.e. the same string shape the retired code already produced. The already-built C# port (src/Marrow.App/Views/Chat/HydraPanel.cs:801-808 Elapsed()) still implements the retired manual formula and, on that reading, would already match B3's new output by coincidence; this needs positive confirmation rather than being assumed. Two doc-comment edits in this file (the file-level intro at :5-11 and the HydraLiveInfo comment now at :475-477) are wording-only and touch no code path; PR-HYDRA-179's source_evidence quotes the old, longer comment prose verbatim, which is now stale text describing the same, unchanged HydraLiveInfo.shown function.
unresolved_questions: Verify the exact `Duration.formatted(.units(allowed: [.seconds, .minutes], width: .narrow, maximumUnitCount: 2, fractionalPart: .hide(rounded: .down)))` output against the compiled B3 app before closing PR-HYDRA-180; this report infers 'Ns'/'Mm Ss' by analogy with the sibling RelativeTime.duration precedent rather than an independent runtime check of this exact call.

files.purpose: Parses a Hydra lead's markdown report-batch message into a structured digest (an optional intro paragraph plus one entry per head with its name/task/outcome/effort/landing/body, dropping the lead's own closing instructions from the last head's body) and renders it as a native-feeling popover: a combined header with overlapping glyphs and totals for several heads, or a head-carrying single header for one head, then one card per head with its landing (files landed / not-landed / nothing changed / unfinished) and its markdown report, collapsed to name+task+landing for multi-head batches until tapped open.
state_owned: expanded: Set<String> (which multi-head cards are open)
blocks: [String: [MarkdownBlock]] (populated eagerly in init for a single head, warmed off-thread for the rest via .task(id: text))
side_effects: `.task(id: text)` calls MarkdownView.warm(...) off the main thread to pre-parse markdown for heads not yet shown
platform_assumptions: PopoverScroll's eager whole-content layout (again, so the popover opens at its final size)
Regex-based line parsing (wholeMatch, range(of:options:.regularExpression)) over the lead's own generated text, Unicode-minus-sign (U+2212) aware for the "+A −D" file suffix
ui_elements: Multi-head header: up to 9 overlapping 22pt glyphs plus a '+N' overflow badge, title, totals line, optional 'still at work' sentence
Single-head header: 24pt glyph with outcome seal, name, outcome+effort caption, files line, task, optional 'still at work' sentence
Per-head cards: collapsible name row with chevron, task, landing rows/file rows, and the report body, 'No report.' placeholder, or a warming spinner
feature_notes: B2->B3 adds "ultra" to parseHeader's fixed set of recognised effort words (now low/medium/high/xhigh/max/ultra/minimal/fast/default -- nine words instead of eight). "Ultra" is a genuine reasoning-effort tier elsewhere in this same B3 tree (ModelOption.effortTitle in Core/Models/Provider.swift capitalises any word it does not special-case, including "ultra"), so a head's header ending in e.g. '(Ultra)' is now correctly peeled off into head.effort and shown as the outcome caption's effort suffix; in B2 the same group fell through as non-meta and stayed stuck in the visible task text instead. PR-HYDRA-199 (status IMPLEMENTED) documents exactly the retired eight-word set, and its already-built C# port (src/Marrow.App/Views/Chat/HydraReportsPopover.cs:147, the `isEffortWord` pattern match) reproduces that same eight-word set verbatim -- so both the spec record and the shipped port code are now one word short of B3 and must add "ultra".
